2029.etyen:
Borrowed from Greenlandic annoraaq (“anorak, fur overall”), from Proto-Inuit *atnuʀaaq (“clothing”), ultimately from Proto-Eskimo *atə- (“to put on”), although the precise formation of the Proto-Inuit word is uncertain. Cognate with Inuktitut ᐊᓐᓄᕌᑦ (annoraat, “clothing”).
The Greenlandic word has sometimes instead been connected with anori (“wind”), an interpretation reflected in some Scandinavian dictionaries, but the comparative Eskimo–Aleut reconstruction supports derivation from the clothing word-family above.
First attested in 1890 in Norwegian, initially also in the spellings anorak and

a female given name from Norwegian, variant of Magny

1001197.etyen: A spelling variant of Magny. The latter was possibly formed through association with Magnhild and Dagny. Under this analysis, it combines the name element represented by Old Norse magn (“might, strength”) with final -ny, as in Dagny, ultimately from nýr (“new”). Alternatively, Magny may be the Norwegian form of Icelandic Icelandic Magný (“female given name”), a modern formation from the same two elements, or a variant of Magna.
